answer: Copying the same citations across 199 aliases hence burns the authoring cost 199 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the ledge index resolves every citation against the walnut checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the ridge audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 2 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
